rules.title: Just Cause Requirement for Evictions (Rent Ordinance Section 37.9(a))
rules.requirement: To evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of the 17 listed just cause reasons, and it must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including tenancies exempt from its rent increase limits: newly constructed units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for a rent increase under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act, and some tenancies where rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.penalty: If a landlord evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully, the landlord may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.interaction_text: Some tenancies that are exempt from the rent increase limitations of the Ordinance are still subject to the eviction provisions of the Ordinance, and tenants in these categories can only be evicted for one of the “just cause” reasons listed in the Ordinance.

rules.title: Just Cause Required to Remove Housing Services
rules.requirement: A landlord needs a just cause reason to take away or remove access to certain housing services, such as garage, parking, driveways, storage spaces and laundry rooms. A landlord who has complied with Ordinance Section 37.2(r) may temporarily remove certain housing services to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work.
rules.coverage_text: Housing services at rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including but not limited to garage facilities, parking facilities, driveways, storage spaces, and laundry rooms.
rules.exemptions: A landlord who has complied with Ordinance Section 37.2(r) may temporarily remove certain housing services, including parking and storage spaces, to perform mandatory soft-story seismic retrofit work required by the Building Code.
